editorial.headline: Building-Material Wholesale: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Foreign ownership is open nationally, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium bars registration of this building-material wholesale activity.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity as a PMA business in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, even though it is nationally open to foreign investment. The activity is wholesale trade in a varied basket of building materials: cement, sand, nails and paint are expressly within its scope. It is the trade function behind supplying construction materials through wholesale channels, rather than a description of a single product line.

The registration is available across the full business-scale range listed in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth is useful context for founders: the classification is framed around the wholesale activity, and the record opens it from the smallest named scale through the largest. The stated examples give the activity its practical shape. A wholesale offer spanning cement, sand, nails and paint sits squarely within the description; the material mix is deliberately broad rather than confined to one of those items.

Nationally, the position is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the national maximum foreign ownership is 100%. Foreign capital can therefore hold the entire national ownership ceiling for this activity. The source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The national signal is full foreign openness, which makes the Bali restriction especially important to read as a location-specific registration outcome rather than as a national ownership limit.

Bali changes the answer completely. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is recorded as Low or Medium-Low across every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s moratorium recorded in May 2026. Under the stated provincial rule, that moratorium blocks PMA registration on an island-wide, permanent basis. Accordingly, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. This is not a reduced Bali foreign-ownership percentage alongside the national 100% ceiling; it is a block on PMA registration in the province. For a founder weighing locations, the decisive distinction is simple: nationally the activity is open, while Bali does not admit PMA registration for it under the stated moratorium.
